points: "The Patient Experience Team is the central point for receiving patient feedback for NHS Lothian."

steps.what: If NHS Lothian’s final complaint answer is not good enough, the independent body is the Scottish Public Services Ombudsman (SPSO). You can only go there after the organisation has given its final decision.
steps.deadline: "We do not normally investigate complaints if you have known about the problem for more than 12 months before complaining."
points: SPSO says: "Make your complaint directly to the organisation."
SPSO says: "Once you have the final decision from the organisation, if you are still not happy, you can then bring your complaint to us."
For NHS complaints, stage two at the organisation should give "a final decision after no more than 20 working days, unless there is clearly a good reason for needing more time."
SPSO says: "We do not normally investigate complaints if you have known about the problem for more than 12 months before complaining."
SPSO may still look at a late complaint if "certain circumstances stopped you from making it earlier."
SPSO’s online route starts with a question wizard asking: "Is your complaint about a Scottish public service?"
requires: NHS Lothian’s final decision on the complaint
steps.appliesIf: You have already complained to NHS Lothian about NHS care and remain unhappy after its final response.
alternatives: SPSO guidance page and leaflets if you do not want to start online
missing: The date NHS Lothian gave its final decision
Whether there were any special circumstances causing delay

steps.what: An adult in Scotland may get legal aid for a medical negligence claim, and can also fund a case by a success fee agreement ('no win no fee'), but not both for the same work at the same time. There is also advice-and-assistance funding for early legal advice if you cannot afford it.
points: mygov.scot says civil legal aid can cover "compensation for injuries or medical negligence".
mygov.scot says: "Use the civil legal aid estimator to see if you could get civil legal aid and what you might need to pay."
The SLAB estimator says: "This estimator helps you work out if you are likely to qualify financially for civil legal aid."
mygov.scot says: "Advice and assistance can help with the costs of legal advice from a solicitor if you can't afford it."
SLAB says: "Legal aid (whether advice and assistance or civil legal aid) is an alternative to funding by way of a success fee arrangement."
requires: A solicitor who does legal aid work if you want to apply for legal aid
steps.appliesIf: An adult medical negligence/personal injury claim in Scotland.
alternatives: Private funding via a success fee agreement instead of legal aid
Advice and assistance for initial advice only
missing: The patient’s income, savings/capital and any benefits for legal-aid eligibility
Whether any solicitor wants to offer a success fee agreement instead of legal aid

steps.what: In Scotland, national clinical guidance for professionals is published through Healthcare Improvement Scotland, including SIGN guidelines. NHSScotland also uses NICE interventional procedures guidance in Scotland.
points: Healthcare Improvement Scotland says: "We are the national authority for the development of evidence-based advice, guidance and standards for health and care professionals."
Healthcare Improvement Scotland says this work "helps to provide safer, more effective care."
On the SIGN page, it says: "We work with health and social care professionals and patients to develop guidelines."
SIGN says: "Our guidelines make recommendations for the best standards of care."
Healthcare Improvement Scotland also says: "All interventional procedures guidance is applicable in Scotland."
steps.appliesIf: Clinical guidance for NHS care in Scotland.
alternatives: Relevant NICE interventional procedures guidance also applies in Scotland.
missing: Which exact wrist, scaphoid-fracture, A&E imaging or missed-fracture guideline you want to compare the care against

steps.what: PASS gives free, independent help to people using NHS Scotland, including support with raising concerns or complaints about NHS care.
points: NHS Lothian says PASS is "an independent service".
NHS Lothian says PASS provides "free, accessible and confidential information, advice and support".
NHS Lothian says PASS can help "from explaining your rights and responsibilities as a patient to helping you write a letter or make a phone call."
steps.appliesIf: You want help understanding your rights or making an NHS complaint in Scotland.
alternatives: NHS Lothian Patient Experience Team can also give confidential advice, but it is part of NHS Lothian, not independent.

sources.quote: PASS is an independent service which provides free, accessible and confidential information, advice and support to patients, their families and carers about NHS healthcare.
They can help you through the process of providing feedback, from explaining your rights and responsibilities as a patient to helping you write a letter or make a phone call.

steps.what: You can ask NHS Lothian for your records through its Request for Records Portal or by sending its Subject Access Request form by email or post. The portal itself needs sign-in or account creation before the request form starts.
steps.wall: The Request for Records Portal asks the user to sign in or create an account before the form starts.
points: NHS Lothian says: "You can request copies of Health Records held by NHS Lothian in the following ways:"
NHS Lothian offers an "Online Portal: Request for Records Portal" and a "Downloadable Form:"
NHS Lothian says: "You can return your forms by email to Loth.sarteam@nhs.scot or by post to:"
The portal route has a wall: you must sign in or create an account before the form starts.
The ICO says: "In most circumstances, you cannot charge a fee to deal with a request."
The ICO says: "You must respond without undue delay, and within one month of receipt of the request."
steps.appliesIf: You want a copy of your own NHS Lothian medical records.
alternatives: Use NHS Lothian’s downloadable Subject Access Request form and return it by email or post instead of the portal
missing: Whether you want to use the portal or the paper/email form
Any ID or extra information NHS Lothian may ask for to find the records
